room_or_space: No room named on the sheet. The sheet shows a first-floor window glazing pattern (elevation of one leaded-glass light) and second-floor window details (interior elevation, vertical section, exterior elevation of the head and sill, with a horizontal section through the jambs); no room, wall or plan context is drawn.

proportions.notable_proportion: As drawn, the first-floor window pattern panel is slightly wider than tall (roughly 11:10). Its central field is a staggered lattice of very shallow lozenges, each roughly three times as wide as it is high, about two lozenges wide and six to seven tiers tall; the top tier is closed by two low-pitched diagonals springing from the upper corners of the field and meeting on the vertical centreline. Side border lights are tall and narrow. No written dimensions; a 0-12 inch graphic bar scale is the only size reference.

layout.organisation: Two groups on one sheet: left, three vertically aligned details of the second-floor window captioned INTERIOR, SECTION and EXTERIOR, each showing the head at the top and the sill at the bottom, interrupted mid-height by a horizontal (plan) section through the jambs drawn across all three; right, the first-floor window glazing pattern drawn as a single rectangular light in elevation, with the captions and title lettering below it.
layout.axes: The window pattern is bilaterally symmetrical about a vertical centreline (a single vertical came divides the top band and the bottom band at centre; the lozenge lattice is centred on it). The three second-floor details share common horizontal datum lines for head, jamb section and sill.

openings.position: Top right of sheet, captioned FIRST FLOOR WINDOW PATTERN; one complete light drawn in elevation
openings.pattern: Leaded (came) glazing pattern of straight lines only, drawn as double lines: a rectangular border; a deep plain band across the top divided once at centre by a vertical came; a shallower plain band across the bottom, also divided at centre; tall narrow border lights down each side, each subdivided into a tall upper light, a long middle light and a pair of small side-by-side lights at the bottom; inside these, columns of small square and rectangular lights stacked either side of the central field; the central field is a diaper lattice of shallow, horizontally elongated lozenges formed by two families of low-pitched diagonals, with half-lozenges meeting the side grids; the two uppermost diagonals spring from the upper corners of the field and meet at the vertical centreline. Some lozenge edges are drawn with a heavier line weight than the rest of the lattice.

openings.position: Left half of sheet, captioned SECOND FLOOR WINDOW DETAILS, shown as INTERIOR elevation (left), SECTION (centre) and EXTERIOR elevation (right), head above and sill below, with a plan section through the jambs across the middle
openings.pattern: Interior elevation: the head and sill are framed by nested, stepped rectangular trim bands (four to five concentric lines) forming a picture-frame surround, with a plain vertical jamb strip. Section: a stepped wood head member with a coved underside and a stop, a thin sash with the glazing drawn as a dotted line, an interior stool and a sloping exterior sill that projects beyond the wall face; stippled fill beyond the wood indicates the wall/plaster. Exterior elevation: the opening is flanked by walls drawn with closely spaced horizontal coursing lines, with a plain head band above and a projecting sill band below. Plan section: hatched jamb members at each side with the sash/stop lines and dotted glass line running between them.
